subject: general
question: Which Buddhist text explains rules made for the Buddhist Sangha?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vinay Pitaka.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 1**, Sutta Pitaka, is **incorrect** as it contains **discourses** and** teachings** of the Buddha.
 
• **Option 3**, Abhidhamma Pitaka, is also **incorrect **as it contains **Buddhist philosophy and psychology. **
 
• **Option 4**, Buddhacharita, is** incorrect **as it is a **biography of the Buddha **written in** Sanskrit** by** Asvaghosa. **
 
• **Option 2,** Vinay Pitaka, is the **correct answer** as it contains the **rules and regulations** for the** monastic community,** including the **conduct of monks and nuns**.
 
 
• It provides **guidelines** for **disciplinary actions** and procedures. 
 
• It is divided into three sections: **Suttavibhanga, Khandhaka, and Parivara.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **three Pitakas (Tipitaka)** are the collections of **Buddhist scriptures **written in the **Pali language **and are considered the most important texts in **Theravada Buddhism.**
